hook.situation: You need to explain a routine, a travel step, or a small mistake in the exact order it happened.
objectives: Use V-고 나서 when one action is finished before the next starts.
Use V-자마자 when the second action happens immediately after the first.
Use sequence words like 먼저, 그다음, 바로, 이미, and 방금 to make the timeline easy to follow.
hook.whyItMatters: Korean sequence is not only 'and then.' Plain -고 can list actions, but -고 나서 highlights completion, and -자마자 highlights no gap. This matters in real messages like 'after I arrive, I will call' versus 'the moment I arrive, I will call.'

grammarNotes.title: V-고 나서 — after finishing, then
grammarNotes.func: V-고 나서 means "after doing V (and finishing it)." It tells the listener that the first action is done before the next one starts. Usually the same person does both actions.

formTable.when: Verb stem ending in a vowel
formTable.ex: 보다 → 보고 나서, 자다 → 자고 나서

formTable.when: Verb stem ending in a consonant
formTable.ex: 먹다 → 먹고 나서, 씻다 → 씻고 나서
놀다 → 놀고 나서, 만들다 → 만들고 나서

formTable.when: Never put past tense on this verb
formTable.add: keep the stem plain — 나서 already means "after"

examples.en: After I eat, I brush my teeth.
examples.note: Eating finishes first, then the next thing starts.

examples.en: After I did my homework, I met a friend.
examples.note: The past tense goes only on the last verb (만났어요), not on 하다.

examples.en: After I wash my hands, I eat.
examples.note: Same person does both — the usual case for -고 나서.

examples.ko: 이 책을 읽고 나서 영화를 볼 거예요.
examples.romanization: i chaek-eul ilkko naseo yeonghwa-reul bol geoyeyo.
examples.en: After I finish this book, I'm going to watch a movie.
examples.note: Works for plans too. 읽고 sounds like [일꼬]. The reading has to finish first.

keyPoint.label: -고 나서 vs. plain -고
keyPoint.body: Plain -고 just links two actions like "and": 밥을 먹고 이를 닦아요 (I eat and brush my teeth). Adding 나서 puts the spotlight on finishing the first one before starting the next. Reach for -고 나서 when you want "after I'm done with this, then that."

grammarNotes.pronunciation: You hear it as [고 나서]. Note that 고 tenses after a stem ending in a stop sound: 먹고 나서 sounds like [먹꼬 나서], 받고 나서 like [받꼬 나서]. After a vowel (보고 나서) it stays soft. Keep 나서 light so it links right on.

drill.instruction: Join the two actions into one sentence with V-고 나서, in the 해요 form.
drill.model: 손을 씻다 + 밥을 먹다 → 손을 씻고 나서 밥을 먹어요.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: "After I ate" feels past in English, so people add -었- to the first verb. But 나서 already carries "after finishing," so the first verb stays a plain stem. Only the last verb shows the real tense.

grammarNotes.title: V-자마자 — as soon as
grammarNotes.func: V-자마자 means "as soon as / the moment V happens." The second thing comes right after the first, with no time in between. The two halves can have the same person or different ones.

formTable.when: Verb stem ending in a vowel
Verb stem ending in a consonant
Never put past tense on this verb
formTable.add: keep the stem plain — tense goes on the second half only

examples.en: As soon as I get home, I wash my hands.
examples.note: No gap — the washing happens the instant you walk in.

examples.en: As soon as the movie ended, I went home.
examples.note: Here the two halves have different subjects (the movie / I).

examples.en: As soon as I got to school, I called my friend.
examples.note: Past tense shows up only on the second verb (전화했어요).

examples.en: As soon as I lay down, I fell asleep.
examples.note: An immediate, almost automatic reaction with no delay.

keyPoint.label: -자마자 vs. -고 나서
keyPoint.body: Both put one action before another, but the timing is different. -고 나서 is "after finishing," and a pause is fine: 밥을 먹고 나서 좀 쉬었어요 (I ate, then rested a bit). -자마자 is "the very moment," no gap at all: 집에 오자마자 잤어요 (got home and went straight to sleep). Use -자마자 only when there's truly no time in between.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: You hear it as [자마자], three even, light beats. After a stem ending in a stop sound it tenses a little: 듣자마자 sounds like [듣짜마자], 눕자마자 like [눕짜마자]. After a vowel (오자마자) it stays soft. No pause before it.

drill.instruction: Join the two actions into one sentence with V-자마자.
drill.model: 집에 오다 + 손을 씻다 → 집에 오자마자 손을 씻어요.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: "As soon as I came home" is past in English, so people add -았/었- to the first verb. In Korean, 자마자 sticks to the plain stem (오-), never a past form. Put the past tense only on the second verb (씻었어요).

exampleSentence.note: Names the next step in a routine.

exampleSentence.en: After getting ready, I left right away.
exampleSentence.note: 바로 pairs naturally with sequence sentences.
Recent completion, not necessarily immediate sequence.

exampleSentence.en: After washing my hands, I eat.
After getting ready, I left right away.
exampleSentence.note: A natural morning or trip step.

exampleSentence.en: After grabbing my wallet, I left.
exampleSentence.note: The departure waits until the previous step is complete.

exampleSentence.en: Please call as soon as you arrive.
After checking the reservation, I went up.

extendedVocabulary.english: to grab; to pack; to take care of

exampleSentence.en: After grabbing my wallet, I left.
I realized I had left my wallet behind.
exampleSentence.note: A realistic reason to return home.

exampleSentence.en: After turning off the light, I closed the door.
After closing the door, I came out.

extendedDialogue.setting: A friend asks about a morning mistake and the steps that followed.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.en: What order did you get ready in this morning?
lines.grammarNote: 순서 sets up a step-by-step explanation.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.ko: 먼저 손을 씻고 나서 아침을 먹었어요.
lines.romanization: meonjeo soneul ssitgo naseo achimeul meogeosseoyo.
lines.en: First, after washing my hands, I ate breakfast.
lines.grammarNote: -고 나서 marks the completed first step.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.en: Then did you leave right away?
lines.grammarNote: 그다음 and 바로 clarify the next step and speed.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.ko: 네, 그런데 집에서 나오자마자 지갑을 두고 온 걸 알았어요.
lines.romanization: ne, geureonde jibeseo naojamaja jigabeul dugo on geol arasseoyo.
lines.en: Yes, but as soon as I came out of the house, I realized I had left my wallet behind.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.en: So did you go back up?

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.ko: 네, 지갑을 챙기고 나서 다시 출발했어요.
lines.romanization: ne, jigabeul chaenggigo naseo dasi chulbalhaesseoyo.
lines.en: Yes, after grabbing my wallet, I left again.
lines.grammarNote: The second -고 나서 marks the fixed next step.

readingText.title: A small morning mistake
readingText.body: 지훈은 아침에 먼저 손을 씻고 나서 아침을 먹었어요. 그다음 불을 끄고 문을 닫고 집에서 나왔어요. 그런데 엘리베이터 앞에 도착하자마자 지갑을 두고 온 걸 알았어요. 그래서 다시 집에 올라갔어요. 지갑을 챙기고 나서 다시 출발했고, 역에 도착하자마자 친구에게 전화했어요. 친구는 이미 예약을 확인하고 기다리고 있었어요.
readingText.bodyTranslation: In the morning, Jihoon first washed his hands and ate breakfast. Then he turned off the light, closed the door, and came out. But as soon as he reached the elevator, he realized he had left his wallet behind. So he went back up. After grabbing his wallet, he left again, and as soon as he arrived at the station, he called his friend. His friend had already checked the reservation and was waiting.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 지훈은 아침을 먹기 전에 무엇을 했어요?
지훈은 언제 지갑을 두고 온 걸 알았어요?
지훈은 지갑을 챙기고 나서 무엇을 했어요?

culturalNote.title: Clear order in practical messages
culturalNote.body: Korean sequence markers are useful for quick explanations: 먼저, 그다음, -고 나서, and -자마자 let the listener follow the order without guessing.
culturalNote.tip: Use -고 나서 for completed steps and -자마자 for immediate next actions, especially in travel, errands, and appointment updates.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence means 'after washing my hands'?
inlineExercises.explanation: The first verb before -고 나서 does not take past tense.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence means 'as soon as I arrived'?
inlineExercises.explanation: -자마자 attaches directly to the verb stem.

inlineExercises.prompt: You want to say there was no delay before calling. Which fits?

inlineExercises.explanation: V-고 나서 means after finishing the first action.
Do not put past tense before -자마자.

inlineExercises.prompt: 밥___ 먹고 나서 출발했어요. (After eating, I left.)
inlineExercises.explanation: 밥 is what you eat, so it takes 을. 먹고 나서 then shows the next action happened after eating.
-자마자 means as soon as the first action happens. 도착하다 becomes 도착하자마자.
-고 나서 makes the first action clearly finished before the second starts. 씻고 나서 comes before 잤어요.
먼저 and 그다음 make the timeline explicit. 준비하고 links the first step before 출발해요.

inlineExercises.prompt: Fix the sentence: '수업이 끝났자마자 집에 갔어요.'
inlineExercises.explanation: -자마자 attaches to the verb stem, not the past form. 끝나다 becomes 끝나자마자.

bullets: V-고 나서 means after finishing the first action: 손을 씻고 나서 밥을 먹어요.
V-자마자 means as soon as, with almost no gap: 도착하자마자 전화했어요.
먼저, 그다음, 바로, 방금, and 이미 help the timeline feel clear.
Do not put tense on the first verb: 도착하자마자, not 도착했자마자.

writingTask.prompt: Describe your morning routine in order: what you do first, then next, and what you do as soon as you arrive.
writingTask.hint: Use V-고 나서 for 'after finishing, then' (씻고 나서), and V-자마자 for 'as soon as' (도착하자마자).
writingTask.model: 먼저 씻고 나서 밥을 먹어요. 그다음에 준비하고 나서 출발해요. 회사에 도착하자마자 메일을 확인해요.
writingTask.modelEn: First I wash up and then eat. After that I get ready and then leave. As soon as I arrive at work, I check my email.

canDo: Order two actions with V-고 나서 (먹고 나서 가요)
Say one thing follows another instantly with V-자마자 (도착하자마자 전화해요)
Sequence a routine with everyday words (먼저, 그다음, 준비하다, 출발하다)
